label: STOPP D16
title: Antipsychotic used as a sleeping medicine
statement: Antipsychotics as hypnotics, unless sleep disorder is due to psychosis or BPSD effects of dementia (not recommended in summary of product characteristics; increased risk of confusion, hypotension, extra-pyramidal side effects, falls).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y
source.credit: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: An antipsychotic taken to help sleep, when the sleep problem is unrelated to psychosis or behavioural or psychological symptoms of dementia, adds a risk of confusion, low blood pressure, stiffness and falls.

medicine_groups.name: Antipsychotics
medicine_groups.note: Tablets and liquids count, as do asenapine sublingual wafers and ziprasidone or cariprazine capsules. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Exclude long-acting depot injections from this oral hypnotic group.

needs_facts.what: Cause of the sleep problem during this antipsychotic course
needs_facts.meets: The record establishes that neither psychosis nor behavioural or psychological symptoms of dementia caused the sleep problem.

options.words: Behavioural or psychological symptoms of dementia
Both psychosis and behavioural or psychological symptoms of dementia
Neither psychosis nor behavioural or psychological symptoms of dementia

needs_facts.what: Use of the antipsychotic for sleep during this course
needs_facts.meets: The directions, a linked prescribing note or a recorded history says this antipsychotic was used for sleep during the course.

options.words: Used to help the patient sleep

rule_for_models: Apply from age 65 at the supply and confirm an unknown age before reporting a STOPP finding. Look for a Group A antipsychotic used as a hypnotic, documented in directions or a linked condition, observation or prescribing note. Bedtime dosing or an unrelated insomnia diagnosis alone does not establish hypnotic use. Assess each dated course and describe a completed course as historical. If neither psychosis nor behavioural or psychological symptoms of dementia caused the sleep problem, report a finding and cite the supply, the evidence of hypnotic use and the cause. If either caused it, report no D16 finding. If the only clue is bedtime-only dosing and the reason is unknown, report only a possible finding and ask whether the medicine was used for sleep. If sleep use is documented but its cause is unknown, report only a possible finding and ask what caused the sleep problem. Low dose, an unrelated insomnia diagnosis or unspecified as-needed directions alone give no D16 finding. A documented use solely for another purpose also gives no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Why the antipsychotic was started, and whether the sleep problem is really caused by psychosis or by dementia. Also the dose actually taken and any medicines from a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Could you review why the antipsychotic was prescribed for this course and, if it is still being used for sleep, whether a safer option would be suitable?
